facts.statement: Huanansaurus lived approximately 72 million years ago during the late Cretaceous period in what is now China.
facts.quote: Huanansaurus is an extinct genus of oviraptorid dinosaur that lived approximately 72 million years ago, between the Campanian and Maastrichtian, during the latter part of the Cretaceous period in what is now China, in the Nanxiong Formation.

facts.statement: Huanansaurus was named and described in 2015 by a team led by Lü Junchang and Pu Hanyong.
facts.quote: In 2015, Lü Junchang, Pu Hanyong, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Xu Li, Chang Huali, Shang Yuhua, Liu Di, Lee Yuong-Nam, Martin Kundrát and Shen Caizhi named and described the type species Huanansaurus ganzhouensis.

facts.statement: The genus name Huanansaurus is derived from Huanan, the historical name for Southern China.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Huanan, "Southern China".

facts.statement: The species name ganzhouensis refers to the fossil's origin in Ganzhou.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the provenance from Ganzhou.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen HGM41HIII-0443 comes from the Campanian-Maastrichtian layers of the Nanxiong Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, HGM41HIII-0443, was found in a layer of the Nanxiong Formation dating from the Campanian - Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partially articulated skeleton including a nearly complete skull, lower jaws, neck vertebrae, forelimb bones, and parts of the hindlimb.
facts.quote: It consists of a partially articulated, incomplete skeleton which includes a nearly complete skull and lower jaws, the first seven neck vertebrae, a humerus, ulna, radius and hand of the right arm, the left hand, the lower part of the right thighbone, the upper part of the right shinbone, and the distal parts of the right foot.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is housed in the Henan Geological Museum in Zhengzhou.
facts.quote: The specimen is part of the collection of the Henan Geological Museum at Zhengzhou.

facts.statement: In 2026, researchers Hao and Xu assigned a new specimen from the Tangbian Formation to Huanansaurus and suggested that Corythoraptor is a junior synonym.
facts.quote: In 2026, Hao and Xu assigned IVPP V34154, probably from the Tangbian Formation, to Huanansaurus and suggested that Corythoraptor is a junior synonym of the former.

facts.statement: A specimen preserved on top of a nest was assigned to Huanansaurus and is held at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
facts.quote: The specimen was donated to the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology and preserved an individual situated on top of a nest.

facts.statement: The species was formally named and described on July 2, 2015, by a team including Lü Junchang and Pu Hanyong.
facts.quote: El 2 de julio de 2015, la especie tipo Huanansaurus ganzhouensis fue nombrada y descrita por Lü Junchang, Pu Hanyong, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Xu Li, Huali Chang, Shang Yuhua, Liu Di, Yuong-Nam Lee, Martin Kundrát y Shen Caizhi.

facts.statement: Huanansaurus is a relatively large oviraptorid with a body length of more than 2 meters.
facts.quote: Huanansaurus es un ovirraptórido bastante grande con una longitud corporal de más 2 metros.

facts.statement: A unique trait of Huanansaurus is that the lower condyles of the quadrate bone are positioned below its upper head.
facts.quote: En el hueso cuadrado los cóndilos inferiores se posicionan por debajo de su cabeza superior.

facts.statement: The first metacarpal is long and slender, with a transverse width equal to one-fifth of its length.
facts.quote: El primer metacarpiano es largo y delgado con una anchura transversal igual a un quinto de su longitud.

facts.statement: The hand claws have prominent lips on the upper rear part of their tips.
facts.quote: Las garras de la mano tienen "labios" prominentes en la parte superior de su extremo posterior.

facts.statement: The temporal opening on the skull roof is round and much smaller than the temporal opening on the side of the skull.
facts.quote: La abertura temporal de la bóveda craneana es redonda y mucho más pequeña que la abertura temporal a los lados del cráneo.

facts.statement: Huanansaurus is classified within the family Oviraptoridae.
facts.quote: familia: Oviraptoridae

facts.statement: Huanansaurus is placed in the subfamily Oviraptorinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Oviraptorinae

facts.statement: Huanansaurus is considered a sister genus to Citipati within the subfamily Oviraptorinae.
facts.quote: Huanansaurus fue situado dentro de Oviraptoridae en la subfamilia Oviraptorinae, como un género hermano de Citipati.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Huanansaurus as Citipatinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Citipatinae

facts.statement: It is debated whether Corythoraptor jacobsi is a synonym of Huanansaurus, as noted in 2017.
facts.quote: synonyms: Corythoraptor jacobsi? Lü et al., 2017

facts.statement: Huanansaurus was one of eighteen dinosaur taxa described in 2015 in open access or free-to-read journals.
facts.quote: Huanansaurus was one of eighteen dinosaur taxa from 2015 to be described in open access or free-to-read journals.

rejected.statement: The holotype skeleton of Huanansaurus was uncovered during the construction of the Ganzhou railway station in Jiangxi province, China.
rejected.quote: The skeleton of a new oviraptorid Huanansaurus ganzhouensis was uncovered during the construction of the Ganzhou railway station in Jiangxi province, China.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'uncovered during the construction of the Ganzhou railway'
